extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology from local XML/PDF/OA figure captions. Direct mechanism labels are limited to assays directly performed in the paper.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Brevinin-1GHd permeabilized bacterial membranes in a SYTOX Green assay; reported permeability reached 100% for S. aureus and E. coli at 1x MIC and for tested bacteria at 2x/4x MIC, with MRSA lower at 1x MIC.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Directly supports membrane permeabilization under assay conditions; does not by itself resolve a detailed pore model.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Time-kill assays showed rapid bactericidal kinetics against E. coli, S. aureus, P. aeruginosa, and MRSA at MIC-scaled peptide concentrations.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Killing kinetics are phenotypic support and are not treated as a standalone molecular mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Brevinin-1GHd inhibited formation of S. aureus/MRSA biofilms and eradicated established biofilms at source-reported micromolar concentrations.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm activity is recorded as phenotype; the paper does not define a specific biofilm molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Circular dichroism supported random coil in aqueous buffer and alpha-helical structure in membrane-mimetic environment, consistent with an amphipathic membrane-active peptide context.

mechanism_claims.limitations: Structural context supports plausibility of membrane activity but is not over-promoted to a direct killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The discussion proposes electrostatic interaction with negatively charged cancer-cell membranes as a possible anti-proliferative mechanism.
mechanism_claims.limitations: This is discussion-level inference; primary cytotoxicity/IC50 data are recorded in activity evidence, not as direct anticancer mechanism proof.
